Nissan Seeks Adventures at 2026 SEMA Show in Las Vegas With Frontier, Pathfinder, Armada Concepts
8 photos
Photo: Nissan
The Japanese automaker says it has an unstoppable "commitment to extreme adventure and off-road thrills" and reveals these prototypes to back the claim at this year’s most important tuning and customization-related event in the United States.
The company has a bunch of cool news: the Formula E Team will enter Season 13 with drivers Oliver Rowland and Zane Maloney, alongside Sam Bird as its reserve and development driver and Abbi Pulling as its rookie and simulator driver for the 2026/27 ABB FIA Formula E World Championship. And we also have important novelties for America.
There’s a new 2027 Nissan Pathfinder Special Edition to mark four decades of SUV heritage that reaches dealerships this month with a starting MSRP of $47,390 with FWD or $49,390 with Intelligent AWD. Also, the all-new 2027 Nissan Rogue Hybrid just went on sale in the US with the all-wheel drive SR with SR Technology Package grade, and its public debut is coming at the 2026 Los Angeles Auto Show, Nov. 20-29. Then there’s also the SEMA Show.
Nissan has initially tapped into the tuning enthusiast culture with the compact and sporty Sentra Spec V concept , a 300-hp compact sedan, as well as two Z models, the Nissan Project NAT2 SCCA Touring 2 and the Datsun S30 Concept. But now it’s time for some adventures off the beaten path. Thus, Nissan also returns to this year’s edition of the SEMA Show with a triumvirate of off-road concepts “that reimagine a new level of capability for the brand's most iconic trucks and SUVs.”
They were designed starting from the Frontier pickup truck, Pathfinder three-row SUV, and Armada full-size SUV and will be on display alongside the street concepts at the Nissan booth, #21521, in Central Hall at the Las Vegas Convention Center, Nov. 3-6. First, the Nissan Frontier Ronin concept is a vision of an “unstoppable off-road truck,” featuring a twin-turbocharged version of Frontier's 3.8-liter V6 engine.
There are also Nissan Titan suspension components to widen the vehicle's track width by 12 inches and lift it by over four inches, plus 35-inch Yokohama Geolandar X-AT tires on prototype 17-inch Nismo Ascend beadlock wheels. Last but not least, a full array of Nismo Off-Road accessories includes rock sliders, driving lights and a spare tire carrier, plus a custom big-brake kit, along with sport bucket seats, additional gauges for the twin-turbo engine and custom seat belts with topographic map-inspired details inside the cabin.
The Nissan Pathfinder celebrates its 40th anniversary, so the XE-V6 Concept taps into the celebrations by taking us back to the original WD21 model featuring retro "XE-V6" badging, red with black, charcoal and silver stripes exterior paint, a custom four-inch suspension lift kit, Yokohama Geolandar off-road tires on 18-inch prototype Nismo wheels, bespoke high-clearance off-road bumpers, a roof rack and plenty of additional accessories, including a rear-mounted swing-out tire carrier.
Last but not least, the Nissan Armada Jungle Patrol Concept is an expedition-style transformation with an open-roof design featuring a tubular roll cage plus inwards-facing seats that make it akin to a real safari vehicle. It rolls on 37-inch Yokohama Geolandar tires with custom long-travel suspension components, steel bumpers and fender flares, plus Nismo Off Road lights. So, what do you think, yay or nay? Also, which one of these three concepts is your favorite and why?
